primary_topics: Farewell tribute by CJP to Ambassador Liu (Chinese Ambassador to the Philippines), December 15, 2011 -- praising his diplomatic achievement in earning Filipino respect and acceptance of Chinese judicial decisions

The unique Philippine acceptance of Chinese court judgments: Filipinos convicted and executed in China for drug offenses; while there were clemency requests, there were no massive protests -- in stark contrast to similar cases in other countries where two Cabinet secretaries had to resign
CJP's personal relationship with Chinese Chief Justice Xiao Yang: 20 years of tours of 20 Chinese cities; two trips hosted by Xiao Yang; CJP's invitation for Xiao Yang to visit the Philippines twice

The claim: Philippine people's acceptance of Chinese court judgments is a testament to the close friendly relations between the two countries, fostered significantly by Ambassador Liu's diplomatic work
sub_topics: CJP's 20 years of China travel: at least 20 cities over 20 years; most memorable were two trips hosted by Supreme Peoples Court President Xiao Yang; toured Beijing, Shanghai, Wuhan, Chongqing and the Three Gorges Dam ('the largest hydro-power project in the world')
Relationship with CJ Xiao Yang: 'close friend'; now also retired; visited the Philippines twice at CJP's invitation; showed both tourist spots and different judicial courts of China
Comparative judicial respect: 'The Chinese judicial system may be different from ours but it works well and renders justice in accordance with Chinese laws, traditions and history'

Philippine acceptance of Chinese drug executions: Filipinos convicted and sentenced to death by the Supreme Peoples Court for drug offenses; 'while there were requests for clemency or postponement of the death sentences, our people nonetheless accepted the judgments rendered and executions undertaken'

Contrast with other countries: 'compare this with the howling, demonstrations and rallies undertaken when Filipinos were convicted and sentenced to death in some other countries. In one instance many years ago, the protests were so virulent that at least two Cabinet members, the secretary of foreign affairs and the secretary of labor, had to resign from their posts'

Ambassador Liu's specific achievement: 'silent work in earning the admiration and esteem of our people leading to their respect and acceptance of the Chinese judicial system and the final judgments of the Supreme Peoples Court, even if such judgments may have meant the loss of life of fellow Filipinos'

Personal farewell note: CJP will miss Ambassador Liu 'not only in the official diplomatic circles but also in the green links of the Manila Golf Club where I see you tee off in the very early mornings before you begin your official work'

stances.claim: Philippine acceptance of Chinese court death sentences against Filipino drug offenders -- 'while there were requests for clemency, our people nonetheless accepted the judgments' -- is a unique diplomatic achievement attributable in significant part to Ambassador Liu's work in building Philippine-China trust. This acceptance is qualitatively different from the mass protests triggered by similar executions in other countries.
stances.rhetorical_move: comparative-acceptance-as-diplomatic-metric: the absence of mass protests as the measure of successful bilateral trust-building, with the two-Cabinet-members-resigned contrast as the benchmark

stances.claim: The Chinese judicial system, though different from the Philippine system, 'works well and renders justice in accordance with Chinese laws, traditions and history.' Mutual judicial respect between different legal systems is possible and is itself a foundation of bilateral friendship -- demonstrated by CJP's 20-year personal relationship with CJ Xiao Yang.
stances.rhetorical_move: comparative-judicial-respect argument: the two different judicial systems as equally legitimate within their own legal contexts
stances.confidence: asserted as a personal observation from 20 years of engagement

notable_anecdotes: CJP and CJ Xiao Yang: over 20 years, CJP toured 20+ Chinese cities on two trips hosted by Supreme Peoples Court President Xiao Yang -- seeing both tourist spots and different judicial courts. Xiao Yang visited the Philippines twice at CJP's invitation. Both are now retired. CJP calls him 'a close friend.'

The two-Cabinet-members resignation: when Filipinos were convicted and executed in unnamed other countries, protests were 'so virulent that at least two Cabinet members, the secretary of foreign affairs and the secretary of labor, had to resign from their posts to own the responsibility.' The contrast with the quiet Philippine acceptance of Chinese executions is stark.

Manila Golf Club early mornings: 'I will miss you not only in the official diplomatic circles but also in the green links of the Manila Golf Club where I see you tee off in the very early mornings before you begin your official work.' -- the most personal note in a diplomatic speech.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered December 15, 2011 as a farewell tribute to Chinese Ambassador Liu, this address by CJP salutes Ambassador Liu for his 'silent work in earning the admiration and esteem of our people leading to their respect and acceptance of the Chinese judicial system and the final judgments of the Supreme Peoples Court, even if such judgments may have meant the loss of life of fellow Filipinos.' CJP draws on 20 years of China travel (at least 20 cities) including two memorable trips hosted by Supreme Peoples Court President Xiao Yang -- now retired and a 'close friend' who has visited the Philippines twice at CJP's invitation. He notes the Philippine judicial and people's acceptance of Chinese court judgments sentencing Filipino drug offenders to death: 'while there were requests for clemency or postponement, our people nonetheless accepted the judgments rendered and executions undertaken' -- a remarkable contrast with unnamed other countries where Filipino executions triggered mass protests so virulent that 'at least two Cabinet members, the secretary of foreign affairs and the secretary of labor, had to resign from their posts.' This acceptance is a testament to the close friendly relations between the two countries and to Ambassador Liu's diplomatic work specifically. CJP closes with a personal farewell: 'I will miss you not only in the official diplomatic circles but also in the green links of the Manila Golf Club where I see you tee off in the very early mornings before you begin your official work.'
